 Landry Shamet amassed 22 points (6-of-8 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), one rebound, one assist and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nets.
 On a night when Mikal Bridges (six points, two rebounds, one steal and one block) shot 1-of-7 from the field, Knicks head coach Mike Brown called on his bench. Shamet led the charge, shooting 4-of-6 from beyond the arc and playing 30 minutes to Bridges’ 16. Shamet’s production isn’t enough to make him worth rostering in 12-team leagues, but he can offer points and three-pointers, as he did on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Mikal Bridges recorded 12 points (5-of-8 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the 76ers. 
 After playing a season-low 13 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls, Bridges appeared to get the message on Friday. He matched his season-high with 12 points and added a few steals for good measure. Bridges’ fantasy value remains low, but Friday’s effort was a step in the right direction. 
 Landry Shamet 
 NYK 
 Guard 
 #44 
 Landry Shamet (ankle) recorded 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), one rebound, five assists, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 In the second game of a back-to-back, a team usually needs more production from its bench, and the Knicks’ reserves answered the call in Chicago. Shamet briefly left the game in the first half after tweaking his right ankle, then hit four three-pointers and scored 12 of his 14 points after halftime. Add in the assists and blocks, and this was a good night for the few who are rostering Shamet. 
 Mikal Bridges 
 NYK 
 Guard-Forward 
 #25 
 Mikal Bridges notched 12 points (4-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons. 
 While we aren’t going to proclaim Bridges “back” after a rough first week, Tuesday’s performance was much needed. He shot 4-of-8 from three against the Pistons, including 2-of-4 in the second quarter. New York outscored Detroit 26-12 in the period, rebounding from a slow start. Bridges can be a valuable fantasy option, but many managers were getting close to the point where they had to seriously consider cutting bait. Tuesday’s performance may buy him a little more time. 
 Josh Hart 
 NYK 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Josh Hart finished Sunday’s loss to the Magic with 13 points (5-of-12 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists, two steals and three three-pointers. 
 While Mikal Bridges (six points, five rebounds, one assist, and one block) continues to offer limited fantasy value, Hart has started strong. The Knicks’ wing posted a strong stat line on Sunday and has been a top-50 fantasy player through the first week of the season. Expecting Hart to sustain that isn’t realistic, given all that he brings to the table. That said, some managers may consider selling high before Week 2. 
 Landry Shamet 
 NYK 
 Guard 
 #44 
 The Athletic’s James Edwards III reports that the Knicks and Landry Shamet have agreed to a four-year deal worth $24 million. 
 While there were reports that multiple teams had interest in offering Shamet a deal when free agency opens on Tuesday night, he’s decided to remain in New York. He’ll receive an average of $6 million per year, which leaves the front office some room to work with as they look to follow owner James Dolan’s directive to avoid the second apron. Shamet was not a consistently impactful fantasy option, but he came up big for the Knicks when they needed him most, including shooting 11-of-12 from three in the Eastern Conference Finals. 
 Mitchell Robinson 
 NYK 
 Center-Forward 
 #23 
 Knicks owner James Dolan said during a radio appearance on Wednesday that, while he wants to bring the team back for another run next season, he wants to avoid the second apron. 
 Fresh off the franchise’s first NBA title in 53 years, the Knicks’ focus has turned to the roster makeup for 2026-27. While Dolan made it clear that he’s fine with writing a check to account for entering the luxury tax, that isn’t the case for the second apron. “If we could bring back the whole team, exactly as it is, why wouldn’t you? But I don’t know if we’re going to be able to, contractually,” Dolan said. “We’re willing to stretch, right. There’s certain things in the NBA that you’d have to be suicidal to do. One of them is called the second apron. Cannot go into the second apron. That’s up to Leon (Rose)...I’ll write as big of a check as possible, but I can’t write a check that goes into the second apron.” This is important because two rotation players, Mitchell Robinson and Landry Shamet, are among the Knicks who will be unrestricted free agents at the end of the month. And Jose Alvarado, who was critical in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, has a $4.5 million player option. The Knicks barely avoided the second apron this season; this task becomes even more challenging this summer. 
 Mikal Bridges 
 NYK 
 Guard-Forward 
 #25 
 Mikal Bridges notched 14 points (5-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in Saturday’s Game 5 win over the Spurs. 
 After totaling nine points in Games 3 and 4 of the NBA Finals, Bridges cracked double figures in Saturday’s series clincher. On a night when Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby shot a combined 4-of-18 from the field, with the former fouling out, Bridges’ contributions were needed, even if they weren’t extraordinary. Looking ahead to next season, his availability is what gives Bridges value, especially in category leagues. However, the 2025-26 regular season may lead to him going a little later in drafts after many managers were burned by his struggles. 
 Mikal Bridges 
 NYK 
 Guard-Forward 
 #25 
 Mikal Bridges had 20 points (8-of-13 FGs), six rebounds, six assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Friday’s Game 2 win over the Spurs. 
 Bridges was excellent on the offensive end in Game 2. He was 7-of-8 from the field to start the game, but was also finding his teammates as he had six assists. Bridges has had one game with at least 20 points in every round of the playoffs. This one certainly came at the right time as the Knicks were able to take a 2-0 series lead on the road. Twice before has a team won the first two games of the NBA Finals on the road and that team went on to win the series each time. 
 Landry Shamet 
 NYK 
 Guard 
 #44 
 Landry Shamet had 16 points (5-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Cavaliers in Game 4. 
 Shamet came off the bench and lit up the Cavaliers for 16 points on six attempts. He was 11-of-12 from behind the three-point line in the Knicks’ four-game sweep of the Cavaliers. Shamet has certainly opened some eyes with his shooting in this series and should continue to play 15-20 minutes per game in the NBA Finals. 
 Mikal Bridges 
 NYK 
 Guard-Forward 
 #25 
 Mikal Bridges tallied 22 points (11-of-15 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks in Saturday’s Game 3 win over the Cavaliers. 
 Bridges continues to shine for the Knicks, who are one win away from a second consecutive series sweep and their first NBA Finals appearance since 1999. During Game 3, the Knicks’ wing did his damage from the mid-range and in the paint. All 11 of Bridges’ makes came within 19 feet of the basket, with nine occurring in the paint. He’s been aggressive, and the approach has paid dividends for the Knicks. Bridges will look to do more of the same in Game 4 on Monday.

 Jalen Smith finished with 13 points (6-of-10 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists and one three-pointers against the 76ers on Monday.
 Smith played through a finger injury and remained in the starting role that he has held all season. This was a decent performance for him during what has been a strong start to the year. However, Nic Claxton (hamstring) is getting closer to making his debut for Chicago. When Claxton is healthy and up to speed, he’ll likely be this team’s starting center. Smith holds value as a temporary starter, but when Claxton returns, Smith’s value will take a big hit.

 Josh Giddey posted a double-double on Monday with 13 points (5-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers against the 76ers.
 Giddey’s scoring struggles continued in this game, but when he has played at least 25 minutes in a game this season, he has dished out at least 10 assists. That trend continued in this game, which ended up being one of his better performances this season. Giddey certainly hasn’t played to his ADP to this point of the year, but outings like this one will certainly help redeem his value.

 Caleb Wilson led the Bulls with 24 points (9-of-17 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, four steals and four three-pointers in a 126-107 loss to the 76ers on Monday.
 Wilson continues to be the star of the show in Chicago, and it has worked out well in fantasy basketball. This was the first game he didn’t record at least one steal and one block, but he made up for it with a career high in steals. He has dished out exactly four assists and scored at least 20 points in three straight games, and he has scored fewer than 20 points in only two games. Plus, he has 13 triples over their last three games. The expectation was that he would be a fantasy stud, but his offensive production wasn’t supposed to be this good this quickly.

 Jay Huff led the Pacers with 22 points (8-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists and two blocks against the Hawks on Monday.
 Huff has been filling in as the starting center for Indiana for the last few games, but that hasn’t always led to starter minutes. However, with only six available players for the Pacers in this game, Huff played a significant role. He started off hot, scoring 17 points in the first half, which helped him lead the team in scoring while setting a new season high for points. He’ll continue starting until Ivica Zubac (ankle) returns, which makes him an intriguing streaming option, even if he has struggled as a starter prior to this game.

 Slawson re-signed with Indiana on a two-way deal in July, and he has ended up being part of the Pacers’ rotation this season. However, his role expanded exponentially in this game due to them only having six available players. Slawson didn’t shoot the ball well, but he did a little bit of everything else in the box score. Slawson was productive in this game, but his role won’t typically be large enough for him to repeat it often.

 Braden Smith started on Monday and finished with 19 points (8-of-13 FGs), four rebounds, 10 assists, three steals, one block, two three-pointers and five turnovers in a 108-104 loss to the Hawks.
 The Pacers only had six healthy players for this game, so everyone that was available played a ton of minutes. That allowed Smith to make the first start of his career, and he took full advantage. Most second-round picks don’t record double-doubles in their first starts, but the special circumstances allowed college basketball’s total assist leader from last season to do just that. Smith is a high-level passer, but he won’t be part of the Pacers’ rotation when the team is healthy. Depending on the injury report ahead of Wednesday’s game, he could end up starting again.

 Cade Cunningham had 33 points (13-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, five steals and four three-pointers in the Pistons’ 124-91 victory over the Hornets on Monday.
 Cunningham has now recorded at least 30 points, at least five rebounds, at least seven assists, at least two steals and at least four three-pointers in two of his last three games. Due to his efficiency and five steals, Monday was the 25-year-old point guard’s best game of the young season so far. With Jalen Duren (hamstring) still sidelined, expect the Pistons to continue to lean on Cunningham even more than they usually do.
